textbookText: Fig: 4.1.10 Carbon Cycle 1. Photosynthesis Carbondioxide of atmosphere and water is utilized by producers during photosynthesis to manufacture carbohydrate. The CO2 thus fixed is partially used by the green plant for their own life processes and the rest is stored as their biomass which is available to the heterotrophs as food. In this way, carbon fixed by producers enters food chain and passes to consumers and decomposers. 2. Respiration It is the process in which food is oxidized to liberate energy, CO2 and water. Some amount of carbon of each trophic level is utilized for cellular respiration and rest of it is again stored as their biomass which may be consumed by another trophic level in food chain. 3. Decomposition After the death of the organisms the decomposers break down the remaining dead organic matter and release the left over carbon back into the atmosphere. 4. Combustion (burning) Under certain conditions dead bodies of organisms undergo partial decomposition to form fossil fuels. On burning, these fossil fuels release carbon dioxide to atmosphere. Forest also makes a large amount of fossil fuel. It acts like carbon reservoirs. They release CO2 by forest fires and burning of firewood to the atmosphere.

NITROGEN CYCLE Nitrogen is one of the essential components of different bio molecules like protein, nucleic acid, amino acid, vitamins etc. These molecules play vital role in living organisms. Nitrogen is abundant in atmosphere (about 78%). However, atmospheric nitrogen is not directly utilized by plants. It should be converted into nitrites, nitrates, ammonia, etc. and available in soil, for uptake by plants.

Fig: 4.1.11 Nitrogen Cycle Nitrogen cycle consists of following steps: 1. Nitrogen fixation The conversion of free atmospheric nitrogen into biologically acceptable form or nitrogeneous compounds is called as nitrogen fixation. This process is of three types:

a. Biological nitrogen fixation It is the process in which atmospheric free nitrogen is converted into nitrogeneous compound by certain microorganisms. These microorganisms may be symbiotic like Rhizobium (present in root nodules of leguminous plant), Nostoc, etc. or free living like Azobactor, Clostridium, etc.

The nitric acid so formed reacts with mineral compounds of the soil to form nitrates

c. Industrial nitrogen fixation In industries, free nitrogen and hydrogen gases react through the Haber’s process to form ammonia. This ammonia serves as a crucial component in the production of nitrogen base fertilizers.

In this process, plants uptake nitrogen from soil though their roots, utilizing it to synthesize organic compounds like amino acids, proteins, nucleic acids, etc. The nitrogen present in the compounds passes to animals in food chain. They form animal protein and nucleic acids.

When organisms die, nitrogen containing compounds within their dead bodies and excretory materials undergo conversion into ammonia by ammonifying bacteria. This process is termed as ammonification. The ammonifying bacteria are Bacillus ramosus, B. vulgaris, etc.
The process of conversion of ammonia into nitrites and later into nitrates is called nitrification. This process takes place by some nitrifying bacteria like Nitrosomonas, Nitrobacter, etc.

It is the process of conversion of ammonia and nitrates of soil into atmospheric free nitrogen. This is the process by which nitrogen compounds present in the soil make their way back to the atmospheric nitrogen. The process is carried out by certain bacteria known as denitrifying bacteria like Bacillus denitrificans, Pseudomonas, etc.
Nitrogen of the soil is washed away to the sea and by leaching deep into the earth to form rock. This nitrogen is released only when the rocks are exposed and weathered.

Succession is like a natural makeover that happens in nature over time. Imagine you have a bare plot of land. At first, it might seem empty, but over time, different plants and animals come in and make it their home. This process of change from bare land to a thriving ecosystem is called succession. It helps the ecosystems grow and develop over time.
